verdict_gate: Parity Honesty Rule 10 is absolute for this review: any fresh held-out whose frozen diff_one --no-oracle exit is nonzero rejects the mechanism. No mechanism-only pass classification or scope waiver was applied.
verdict_reason: Multiple fresh valid held-outs returned nonzero from diff_one --no-oracle. java_model: Link.idCommentForSvg at Link.java:106-114 selects entity1/entity2 getName() and the to/backto/association delimiter; Link.commentForSvg at lines 116-120 uses the same raw local names.
Entity.getName at Entity.java:682-684 delegates to Quark.getName. Quark.java:84-90 keeps getName() as the local raw quark name and getQualifiedName() as a separate nested identity.
UGroup.put at UGroup.java:57-72 projects non-word punctuation to dots only in the group metadata channel. It does not redefine Link.idCommentForSvg identity.
The Java SVG serializer escapes attribute syntax after the raw model identity is chosen, as shown by the ampersand counterexample's serialized & and XML parser's recovered raw value.
rust_model: The implementation commit removes own_qname projection and derives oracle candidates, comments, and no-oracle path base IDs from DeploymentConnection.from/to. That causal change matches Java's raw endpoint-name selection.

render_connection at deployment.rs:3671 and the no-oracle link emitter use SvgBuilder.raw formatting. The raw identity value is therefore inserted directly into XML syntax instead of passing through an attribute escaper.

The frozen output proves the ID is model-produced rather than post-hoc surgery: path IDs and link comments arise during render emission, duplicate IDs are uniquified by the normal ID path, and no generated SVG is read back or rewritten.
fixture_shape_and_tuning_audit: No golden-data reads, include_str/include_bytes fixture embedding, checker label branches, fixture names, per-branch-count constant ladders, coordinate-keyed rewrites, comparator changes, or post-render SVG mutation were found in the implementation diff.
The identity implementation adds no parity-affecting numeric constant. Candidate selection is endpoint/order/type shaped and source-line fallback was pre-existing.
Use of svg.raw is ordinary direct emission, not post-hoc surgery, but it is also the immediate cause of the unescaped attribute counterexample.

findings.title: Raw endpoint identity is not safely serialized as SVG attribute data
evidence: checker_xml_ampersand_raw_identity.svg contains id="Gate & Relay-to-Sink-3" and is well-formed XML.
checker_xml_ampersand_raw_identity.rust.svg contains id="Gate & Relay-to-Sink-3" and xmllint reports xmlParseEntityRef: no name.
checker_xml_ampersand_raw_identity.diff.stderr.txt reports failed to parse SVG: malformed entity reference at 16:73; .diff.exit.txt is 101.
identity-trace-attempt-2.stdout.txt records java xml_valid=true, rust xml_valid=false, and the same recovered raw identity on both sides.
findings.cause: The model change correctly switches identity selection from projected names to raw connection endpoint names, but direct svg.raw attribute formatting omits the serializer step that Java applies after selecting that raw identity.

findings.title: Additional valid fresh held-outs are nonzero under the governing comparator
findings.cause: The preserved diffs expose full-render differences under the requested collision, style, order, and reversal axes. Rule 10 makes each nonzero result independently rejecting; none was removed or reclassified.

residues: The valid nested broad-owner control with child endpoints is comparator-clean and the XML trace confirms raw local path identity rather than owner-qualified layout identity.
Other valid inputs retain matching comments/path IDs while differing in parser dispatch, route geometry, or style. These are recorded as rejecting nonzero held-outs, not described as out of scope.
Four exploratory owner-link forms are invalid in the pinned Java oracle. Their sources and all outputs remain preserved, but the rejection rests on multiple valid inputs.
No Cargo, rustc, no-oracle bypass, comparator modification, baseline update, fixture exemption, or artifact deletion was used.
